notes: Unfilled on purpose, and unusually: the statute is readable and the entire agency is not. ORS 56.140, Fees; waiver; rules, was read in full from the Legislature's own copy of chapter 56 and it is a closed list - $100 for each formation document including 'Articles of organization delivered for filing under ORS 63.051', $100 for annual reports, $275 for foreign registrations, $50 for any other document delivered as part of the business registry functions, $20 for service of process. What makes it more than an ordinary fee list is subsection (5): the Secretary of State's power to add fees by rule reaches only copying and certifying records and, in subsection (8), computer lists and terminal access. Nothing in the section authorises a charge for speed, and ORS chapter 63 carries no fee section of its own. That is a strong statutory 'no' and it is deliberately not recorded as one, because Oklahoma already produced the counterexample this namespace has to respect: a $25 same-day service that exists as agency practice with no statute behind it, printed only on the office's own form packet. Oregon's form packets and fee schedule are exactly what could not be reached. Reachability, measured today on the VPN-up route and cross-checked against the routing plan's two-profile run: sos.oregon.gov resolves correctly - the local resolver and Cloudflare DoH agree on 206.16.21.81 and 199.107.32.78, so this is not the router hijack - and establishes no TCP connection to either address, on 443 or on 80, with the VPN up or down. It is dead everywhere rather than route-dependent, so there is nothing to retry. secure.sos.state.or.us, the Oregon Business Registry and the host that serves the Oregon Administrative Rules, answers 200 with the VPN up and serves an F5 shape ('bobcmn', /TSPD/) JavaScript challenge instead of a page - the same shape New York and Washington show. Between them those two hosts carry every Corporation Division page, the business registry fee schedule PDF, the LLC forms and the administrative rules. www.oregonlegislature.gov answers normally, which is why the statute could be read at all; www.oregon.gov/business is a portal stub that links into the dark host and states nothing. Oregon therefore belongs in a browser batch, not in a retry.
needsReview: Every expedite field and every standard-processing field. Blocked by the network, not by absence of a source: sos.oregon.gov makes no TCP connection on either route (dead in both, not route-dependent) and secure.sos.state.or.us answers a scripted client with an F5/TSPD challenge page. What to read in a browser session: (1) sos.oregon.gov/business/Documents/business-registry-forms/br-fee-schedule.pdf, the Corporation Division's fee schedule, for any expedited line; (2) the Articles of Organization form and its instructions, which is where Oklahoma's unstatutory same-day charge turned up; (3) sos.oregon.gov/business/Pages/corporation-division-help.aspx for a stated turnaround; (4) the Oregon Administrative Rules chapter for the Corporation Division on secure.sos.state.or.us/oard, to see whether any fee rule adds what ORS 56.140 does not authorise.

sources.title: ORS 56.140, Fees; waiver; rules - consulted in full in the Legislature's chapter 56 file; $100 per formation document including articles of organization under ORS 63.051, $275 foreign, $50 for any other business registry document, and a rulemaking power in subsections (5) and (8) limited to copies, certificates, lists and terminal access. No expedited-service fee and no authority to set one by rule
ORS chapter 63, Limited Liability Companies - consulted in full for a fee or expedited-service provision; the chapter contains neither and leaves fees to ORS 56.140
